Zoologiste autrichien, né à Vienne. Il m: Austrian zoologist, born in Vienna. Through conditioning he showed that bees see colours, then decoded their waggle dance, published in 1927 and disputed at first. He shared the 1973 Nobel Prize with Konrad Lorenz and Nikolaas Tinbergen.
Législateur athénien. En 508 av. J.-C.,: Athenian lawgiver. In 508 BC, he replaced the kinship-based tribes with ten tribes based on place of residence and enlarged the council from 400 to 500 members. He introduced the selection of citizens by lot for public offices and called his reforms isonomia, equality before the law.
Médecin et mathématicien né à Pavie, jou: Physician and mathematician born in Pavia, a dice and chess player always short of money. Around 1564, he wrote the first systematic treatise on probability, published in 1663. His Ars Magna of 1545 published the solution of cubic and quartic equations. Arrested by the Inquisition in 1570, he ended up with a pension from the pope.
Mathématicien de Bâle, aîné d'une dynast: Mathematician from Basel, eldest of a dynasty of scholars. In 1683, he came across the number e while studying compound interest. He proved the law of large numbers, his "golden theorem", published in 1713, eight years after his death. His rivalry with his brother Johann erupted in the learned journals.
Charpentier né dans le Yorkshire, horlog: Carpenter born in Yorkshire, clockmaker in his spare time. He spent his life building marine timekeepers, from H1 to H4, to win the longitude prize. In 1761-1762, his H4 watch was only five seconds slow in Jamaica. He received 23,065 pounds in all, after the support of King George III.
Écrivain et philosophe né à Langres. Emp: Writer and philosopher born in Langres. Imprisoned at Vincennes in 1749, he edited the Encyclopédie, with d'Alembert and then alone after 1759. In 1766, Catherine II bought his library for 15,000 livres and paid him to remain its keeper.
Officier de marine et savant français. I: French naval officer and scientist. As early as 1770 he formulated a ranked voting method that bears his name. He built the standard metre based on Delambre and Méchain's measurement of the meridian, and improved the reflecting circle. His name is among the 72 engraved on the Eiffel Tower.
Philosophe écossais né à Kirkcaldy. Il p: Scottish philosopher born in Kirkcaldy. He published The Theory of Moral Sentiments in 1759, then The Wealth of Nations in 1776, the founding text of political economy. His contemporaries described him as comically absent-minded: he is said to have brewed buttered bread in a teapot.
Psychiatre né à Bucarest, passé par Vien: Psychiatrist born in Bucharest, who spent time in Vienna, where he invented psychodrama with his Theatre of Improvisation. Settled in the United States, he tested sociometry at Sing Sing prison in 1931, then published Who Shall Survive? in 1934, with some of the first sociograms. He was a pioneer of group psychotherapy.
Psychologue né à Mogilno, dans l'actuell: Psychologist born in Mogilno, in present-day Poland, who settled in the United States in 1933. At the University of Iowa, he compared autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire climates with Lippitt and White. He coined the terms action research and group dynamics, and summed up behaviour in a formula: B = f(P, E), the person and their environment.
Psychologue social né à Ödemiş, en Turqu: Social psychologist born in Ödemiş, Turkey. In 1935, he showed with the autokinetic effect that a group produces its own norms. In 1954, with Carolyn Wood Sherif, he pitted two gangs of boys against each other at Robbers Cave, then reconciled them through common goals. From this he drew realistic conflict theory.
Zoologiste né à Périgueux, grand spécial: Zoologist born in Périgueux, a leading specialist of termites. In 1959, he named stigmergy their way of coordinating through the traces of their work. He edited a huge Traité de zoologie and opposed neo-Darwinism in Evolution of Living Organisms (L'Évolution du vivant), in 1973.
Politiste née à Los Angeles. Dans Govern: Political scientist born in Los Angeles. In Governing the Commons, in 1990, she showed that communities manage pastures, forests, fisheries and irrigation sustainably through their own rules. In 2009, she was the first woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics, with Oliver Williamson.
Mathématicien et météorologue américain,: American mathematician and meteorologist, a weather forecaster for the Air Force during the Second World War, then a researcher at MIT for his whole career. His 1963 paper founded chaos theory. His 1972 talk about the butterfly in Brazil gave the butterfly effect its name.
